name: Capacitor-Grade BOPP/Dielectric Films
scope: Ultra-thin metallised BOPP/PET dielectric film for film capacitors (EV inverters and chargers, solar/wind inverters, grid capacitor banks, drives) and the Indian listed companies making, buying or adjacent to it.

summary.one_line: Main news this week: SRF said on its 22 Oct Q2 FY27 call that its capacitor-grade film already has key customer approvals and is selling ahead of the timeline it first gave, at a significant premium to standard film. A second line is 'likely sooner than later'. That makes SRF the most aggressive new domestic competitor for Xpro India, Cosmo First and JPFL. There was no new ECMS tranche, and the PET-film anti-dumping duty has still not been notified.
key_points: New this week: on its 22 Oct 2026 Q2 FY27 call, SRF said capacitor-grade film 'has scaled up well', has key customer approvals, and that commercial sales are 'progressing well ahead of initially anticipated timelines', at 'a significant premium to vanilla film' (S24). Management also said a second capacitor-film line is 'likely sooner than later given strong traction' (S25).

SRF also has key-customer approvals for aluminium foil used in capacitors and expects commercial sales from Q3 FY27 (S24). Revenue of its Performance Films & Foil segment rose 51% YoY to Rs 2,122 cr in Q2 FY27 (S25). In July, ICICI Direct had expected commercial capacitor-film sales only during FY27, with near-full utilisation by Q1-Q2 FY28 (S10).

IndexBox (28 Sep 2026) forecasts 6-9% annual growth in global dielectric capacitor-film demand over 2026-2035 (7.5% base case), with automotive power electronics growing fastest at 10-14% a year (S1).

Xpro India remains the only listed company that reports dielectric film separately: FY26 sales were Rs 135.52 cr on 3,541 MT (S18). Its Barjora line, commissioned 27 Mar 2026, doubled Indian capacity to 8,000 MT/yr, and it targets 13,000 MT by 2027 including a 5,000 MTPA UAE line (S18, S19). Q2 FY27 results are not yet out.

Cosmo First's website, re-checked on 24 Oct, still rates its capacitor metalliser at 900 MT/yr and says the second metalliser is still being prepared (S3). The Dec 2023 launch was at ~750 MT/yr in 2.5-12 micron (S2).

JPFL Films (Jindal Poly) has 5,000 TPA of capacitor-film capacity operational per CRISIL, which has the company's ratings on Watch Negative (S8). The Rs 250 cr doubling announced in 2024 (S4) is still not confirmed as complete, and a SEBI show-cause notice dated 6 Aug 2026 is open (S7).

Valuations have fallen since our last edition (Screener, 24 Oct). Xpro trades at 68.8x P/E (S20), Cosmo at 11.3x (S15) and SRF at 30.0x (S17); Jindal Poly is loss-making at 1.06x book (S16). All four are 26-39% below their 52-week highs (S15, S16, S17, S20).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: SRF has the clearest positive news this week: commercial capacitor-film sales are running ahead of plan at a premium price, and a second line is likely (S24, S25). The film is still small next to Rs 18,265 cr of trailing group sales (S17).

Xpro India has the most direct exposure: dielectric film was Rs 135.52 cr of FY26 sales (S18), with capacity rising to a 13,000 MT target by 2027 (S19). At 68.8x P/E (S20), the market already prices much of this in.
Cosmo First's 'series' metallised grade targets drives, renewable inverters, UPS and EVs (S3). At 11.3x P/E and 1.17x book (S15), the stock shows no capacitor premium.

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Domestic supply is ramping up quickly. SRF is already selling and plans a second line (S25), Xpro is going to 13,000 MT (S19), JPFL runs 5,000 TPA (S8) and Cosmo plans a second metalliser (S3). No source we found quantifies domestic demand, so prices could fall as these lines fill.
Polypropylene resin is 50-65% of production cost, and China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1).
Jindal Poly: an open SEBI notice (S7), ratings on Watch Negative (S8) and a trailing net loss of Rs 991 cr (S16).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Xpro India and Cosmo First Q2 FY27 results (dates not yet found): Barjora ramp-up and the UAE line (S18, S19); any capacitor-film disclosure from Cosmo (S21).
Whether SRF's board approves a second capacitor-film line (S25), and its first capacitor-foil sales in Q3 FY27 (S24).
Commissioning of Cosmo's second metalliser (S3) and confirmation of JPFL's doubling (S4, S8).
Finance Ministry notification of DGTR's Sep 2026 PET-film anti-dumping recommendation (S22). We found none as of 24 Oct, and none covers BOPP.

blocks.text: Capacitor-grade film is an ultra-thin dielectric film (the insulating layer between a capacitor's plates), mostly biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP). It is vacuum-metallised with aluminium or aluminium-zinc and wound into film capacitors. Cosmo First makes it in clean-room conditions with micro-slitting, at 2.5-12 micron, for AC and DC capacitors (S2). Xpro India makes 2-16 micron base film in standard and high-temperature grades, including ultra-thin, hazy and semi-rough films for power capacitors, EV systems and railways (S18). Packaging BOPP is thicker and has none of these purity or surface requirements. The thin metal layer also gives self-healing: a local short burns the metal away instead of destroying the capacitor.

Demand is moving to thinner films that withstand higher voltages: IndexBox cites 2-4 micron grades for automotive use, especially 800-volt EV platforms. It expects BOPP to keep 60-70% of volume and metallised film to account for 40-50% of value (S1). Cosmo's metallised grades run from Al-Zn standard (fans, motor-run and AC capacitors) to slope/RMF (APFC panels, wind turbines) and 'series' grades (drives, renewable inverters, UPS, EVs) (S3). Xpro calls demand 'structural, not cyclical', driven by electrification, renewables, grid modernisation and traction (S18).

blocks.caption: Third-party forecasts (each is the publisher's own forecast)
rows: PP resin 50-65% of production cost; China 35-45% of global capacity

blocks.text: Last week we also showed Mordor Intelligence's forecast for finished plastic film capacitors (4.86% CAGR, 2026-31). We did not re-verify it this week, so it is left out. Future Market Insights' figure could not be opened in either week.

When it launched in Dec 2023, Cosmo said capacitor film was largely imported from China and saw room for both import substitution and exports (S2). China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1). Xpro calls itself the first-mover domestic producer (S18). We still found no official tonnage series for India's capacitor-film imports.

DGTR's final findings (29-30 Sep 2026) recommend anti-dumping duties of USD 54-366/t on PET film from Bangladesh, China and Thailand (S22). They take effect only if the Finance Ministry notifies them, and as of 24 Oct we found no notification. The case covers PET film, not BOPP, which is the main capacitor dielectric (S1).

blocks.text: After the Aug 2026 tranche, ECMS had 106 approved applications with Rs 69,548 cr of investment, and 38 plants were producing (S13). Metallisers and capacitor makers approved under the scheme add domestic demand for base film. We found no new tranche in the two weeks to 24 Oct.

blocks.text: SRF (updated this week): on the Q2 FY27 call, management said capacitor-grade film is 'already commercialized, we are selling', at 'a significant premium to vanilla film', with key customer approvals in hand. Sales are ahead of the original timeline (S24). It also has key-customer approvals for capacitor aluminium foil, with sales expected from Q3 FY27 (S24). A second capacitor-film line is 'likely sooner than later given strong traction' (S25). Revenue of the Performance Films & Foil segment (the renamed packaging films business) rose 51% YoY to Rs 2,122 cr (S24, S25). SRF does not disclose capacitor-film revenue separately.

Xpro India: FY26 dielectric volume was 3,541 MT versus 3,556 MT in FY25, with net sales of Rs 135.52 cr versus Rs 136.34 cr. Volumes were flat because the new line started only at year-end (S18). FY26 PAT was Rs 30.52 cr (S19). Q2 FY27 results, the first full test of the Barjora ramp-up, are still due.

Cosmo First: in Q1 FY27, net revenue was Rs 1,166 cr and net debt Rs 1,166 cr (2.3x EBITDA). The company says its capex cycle is complete (S21). It discloses no capacitor-film revenue, and its website still describes the second metalliser as forthcoming (S3).

Jindal Poly Films: CRISIL says JPFL has 5,000 TPA of capacitor capacity operational after the May 2025 Nashik fire, and that the loss of profits is not covered by insurance (S8). Screener shows a trailing net loss of Rs 991 cr and June-quarter sales down 23.9% YoY (S16).
Xpro India is the only one of the four that reports capacitor-film volume and revenue separately. Any capacitor-film share for SRF, Cosmo or Jindal Poly is an estimate.

items: Universal Cables makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and power-factor panels, so it is a potential domestic film buyer (S5). We found no disclosed film-supply tie-up.
Polyplex lists electrical insulation among its BOPET uses, but we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S23). The PET-film anti-dumping case matters more for it (S22).
UFlex / Flex Films makes BOPP, BOPET, CPP and metallised packaging films; we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S14).
Garware Hi-Tech Films makes polyester film for electrical and motor insulation at 10-350 micron (S6), thicker than the 2-16 micron capacitor band (S18).

blocks.text: Coverage gap: the main domestic film-capacitor makers (TDK India, Vishay India) and the ECMS metallisers (Dhruv, Capfilm) are unlisted or not confirmed as listed (S12, S13). The listed producers are small caps (Xpro, Cosmo, Jindal Poly) plus one large cap (SRF) where the business is small. We found no mid-cap pure play.

sections.title: Research house views and market pricing

subsections.title: Has the market priced it in?

blocks.title: Price-to-book of confirmed capacitor-film producers, 24 Oct 2026

blocks.text: Compared with our 12-13 Oct snapshot, Screener prices are lower for Xpro (1,047 to 968), Cosmo (813 to 719) and SRF (2,520 to 2,310), and higher for Jindal Poly (647 to 739) (S15, S16, S17, S20). We found no capacitor-specific news behind these moves. Only Xpro, the one producer with large, disclosed exposure, trades at a theme-style multiple (S20). We could not confirm 6- and 12-month returns from a source we opened, so they are left out.

Broker and media coverage is still thin. ICICI Direct's 24 Jul 2026 SRF note discusses capacitor-grade BOPP only as part of SRF's shift to specialty films (S10). This week's SRF coverage (S24, S25) is call write-ups that mention capacitor film alongside chemicals and battery foil. We found no Indian broker note built around capacitor film.

items: Resin cost: polypropylene is 50-65% of production cost (S1).
Chinese overcapacity: China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1), and most imports came from China (S2).

Domestic supply build-out: SRF is selling ahead of plan and may add a second line (S24, S25), Xpro is going to 13,000 MT (S19), JPFL runs 5,000 TPA (S8) and Cosmo plans a second metalliser (S3). That is a lot of new supply against domestic demand no source quantifies.
Small share of revenue: packaging-film cycles dominate earnings at Cosmo, Jindal Poly and SRF (S15, S16, S17).
Governance: Jindal Poly faces a SEBI show-cause notice dated 6 Aug 2026 (S7), and CRISIL has its ratings on Watch Negative (S8).
An SRF board decision on a second capacitor-film line (S25), and first capacitor-foil sales in Q3 FY27 (S24).
Xpro's Q2 FY27 dielectric volumes, and the trial run and commissioning of its UAE line (S18, S19).
Commissioning of Cosmo First's second metalliser (S3) and of JPFL's capacitor-film doubling (S4, S8).
ECMS metallised-film projects (Dhruv, Capfilm) coming on stream, and any new ECMS tranche (S12, S13).
Localisation of EV and solar inverters, the segment IndexBox expects to grow 10-14% a year (S1).
Notification of the PET-film anti-dumping duty (S22). No capacitor-BOPP-specific trade action has been found.

companies.name: SRF Ltd
companies.role: Commissioned a capacitor-grade BOPP plant at Indore on 15 May 2026, phase 1 ~Rs 277 cr (S9). It holds an ECMS approval for a Rs 496 cr capacitor PP-film project (S11) and has been selling commercially since securing key customer approvals (S24).
companies.impact: Sales are ahead of plan at a premium to standard film, and a second line is likely (S24, S25). This is small within group sales of Rs 18,265 cr (S17), but SRF is the fastest-scaling new domestic competitor.

companies.name: Xpro India Ltd
companies.role: Dedicated BOPP dielectric (capacitor) base-film maker at Barjora, West Bengal, making 2-16 micron grades. FY26 dielectric sales were Rs 135.52 cr on 3,541 MT (S18), and capacity doubled to 8,000 MT in Mar 2026 (S19).
companies.impact: Has the most direct exposure, with a 13,000 MT target by 2027 (S19). The stock trades at 68.8x P/E (S20) while SRF is scaling faster than planned (S24).

companies.name: Cosmo First Ltd
companies.role: Makes metallised capacitor-grade BOPP: launched Dec 2023 at ~750 MT/yr in 2.5-12 micron (S2); the metalliser is now rated 900 MT/yr, with a second being prepared (S3).
companies.impact: Capacitor film is undisclosed, and earnings follow packaging film (S21). The stock trades at 11.3x P/E (S15).

companies.name: Jindal Poly Films Ltd
companies.role: Its subsidiary JPFL Films makes capacitor film: 5,000 TPA is operational per CRISIL (S8), and a Rs 250 cr doubling was announced in 2024 (S4).
companies.impact: Fire recovery, a Rs 991 cr trailing loss and the open SEBI notice outweigh the capacitor theme (S7, S8, S16).

companies.name: Universal Cables Ltd
companies.role: Makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and APFC panels (S5).
companies.impact: A potential domestic film buyer as local supply grows; no film-supply tie-up has been disclosed (S5).

companies.name: Polyplex Corporation Ltd
companies.role: BOPET film maker that lists electrical insulation among its industrial uses (S23).
companies.impact: Adjacent only: no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S23). The PET-film anti-dumping case is more relevant to it (S22).

companies.name: UFlex Ltd
companies.role: Its Flex Films business makes BOPP, BOPET, CPP and metallised films (S14).
companies.impact: Has metallising know-how, but we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S14).

companies.name: Garware Hi-Tech Films Ltd
companies.role: Makes polyester film for electrical and motor insulation at 10-350 micron (S6).
companies.impact: Its range sits above the capacitor-film thickness band (S18), so the theme does not currently apply.

method: Weekly refresh of the 2026-W42 edition, researched on 24-25 Oct 2026 with web search and page fetches. New this week: SRF's Q2 FY27 results and its 22 Oct earnings call, read through the Investing.com transcript and the GuruFocus/Yahoo highlights. The NSE press release and the BSE presentation timed out or were blocked, so capacitor-film statements are quoted from the transcript coverage. Re-checked: Cosmo's capacitor-film page (still 900 MT/yr, second metalliser forthcoming); ECMS (no tranche after Aug 2026 found); the PET-film anti-dumping case (no Finance Ministry notification found as of 24 Oct); Jindal Poly/SEBI (no reply or settlement found); Xpro India (Q2 FY27 results not yet published). Valuations are today's Screener figures supplied with the edition (24 Oct 2026). Dropped this week: the Mordor forecast (not re-verified) and the separate April 2026 SEBI-notice article, to keep the source list tight. Not stated as fact because not confirmed: SRF capacitor-film revenue or capacity of a second line, JPFL's capacitor doubling, Cosmo's second-metalliser date, 6- and 12-month stock returns, and Indian capacitor-film import tonnage. Source IDs were renumbered from last week. Some company-website dates are access dates. Companies are classed 'other' unless a company or primary source confirms capacitor-grade production. No ratings or price targets are given.
